value.label: Prescient Euclidean updates: quadratic geometry and both Theorem15.30 bounds
value.plain: Knowing the current loss before output removes the positive gradient-energy term and retains negative squared movement. The initial comparator potential can still make the total bound positive. Finite-dimensional real inner-product E with NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace ℝ E and FiniteDimensional ℝ E. V is closed, nonempty and convex. Played EReal losses have no bottom anywhere, are finite on V, and have ambient global supports at every point of V. Each supplied x(t+1) actually attains the squared-distance-penalized minimum on V; initialization x(0)=x0 is fixed. x0 need not belong to V. There is no affine, smooth-loss, globally finite-loss, bounded-gradient or bounded-domain restriction.
value.fallback: Quadratic Bregman divergence is half squared distance. Variable steps use the maximum previous-state potential divided by the last used step; fixed steps use initial potential. Both subtract exact half-weighted squared movements.
value.relationship: Chapter2 PDF26 points to Algorithm15.8 and Theorem15.30 on PDF277–278. Both branches are mandatory, including the fixed proof left as an exercise on PDF278. Specialize X=univ and psi=norm²/2; interior, derivative, strict-convexity and closedness facts are derived rather than added as user premises. The author’s constrained optimality/global-support step on PDF277 retains an unresolved source-proof justification. The alternative proximal-comparison route does not certify or erase that claim. This is unmerged and unpublished.

contract.model: Receive the entire current loss before choosing the new point and pay that loss at the new point. Lean loss t and eta t are source round t+1: center x(t), output/paid point x(t+1). This differs from ordinary OGD, which scores loss t at x(t). The conclusion identifies the SAME partial Option iterate at every prefix; it is conditional on attained updates and does not assert universal existence.
contract.assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product E with NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace ℝ E and FiniteDimensional ℝ E. V is closed, nonempty and convex. Played EReal losses have no bottom anywhere, are finite on V, and have ambient global supports at every point of V. Each supplied x(t+1) actually attains the squared-distance-penalized minimum on V; initialization x(0)=x0 is fixed. x0 need not belong to V. There is no affine, smooth-loss, globally finite-loss, bounded-gradient or bounded-domain restriction.
contract.parameters: Variable: T>0, every used step positive, adjacent played steps nonincreasing, max indices0..T-1, last eta(T-1). Fixed: eta>0 and any T including0.
contract.regret: R_T(u)=sum_{t<T}((loss t (x(t+1))).toReal-(loss t u).toReal), for every u in V; scoring is finite on V.
contract.guarantee: Each endpoint concludes canonical Option-run equality AND its full signed bound. The shared geometry theorem computes the actual derivative and exact ordered divergence; on complete real Hilbert space it is an explicit generalization of source Euclidean geometry.

value.title: Prescient Euclidean geometry: the quadratic derivative and divergence
value.plain: Complete real Hilbert E: NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace ℝ E, CompleteSpace E; arbitrary x,y. Actual gradient y and exact divergence identity form one conjunction.
value.intuition: The tangent plane of the quadratic leaves exactly half the squared distance between the two points.
value.why: One of three declaration-bound parts of the same prescient Euclidean lesson.
value.position: Algorithm15.8/Theorem15.30, PDF277–278; C2 pointer PDF26. Quadratic X=univ specialization; fixed proof exercise remains mandatory. The author’s constrained optimality/global-support step on PDF277 retains an unresolved source-proof justification. The alternative proximal-comparison route does not certify or erase that claim.
value.proof_idea: Differentiate psi(z)=||z||²/2 to obtain the actual gradient y at y. Substitute the resulting derivative into the shared divergence and expand the squared norm to get Bpsi(x;y)=||x-y||²/2. This geometry theorem makes no algorithm-run conclusion.
